[spoiler=[b]In the South[/b]]

The drone and cruise missile attack from the Bobians would be swiftly dealt with. THOR systems hit the drones with high powered microwaves to fry their electronics making them plunk harmlessly onto the ground. The cruise missiles meet the FAS-3 interceptors which utilize their wide range of radars along with infrared tracking to hunt them down. Ultimately two cruise missiles would make it through the air defenses causing minor damage at Neudresden Port. 

The malware has zero effect on the missile control systems. They are air gapped and completely cut off from the internet making malware hijacking them extremely difficult. The Bobian malware is largely prevented from accessing the Reichswehrs systems. Firewalls and intrusion detection systems quickly alert the military to any breaches allowing for quick responses. At the same time sensitive networks such as communications and autonomous system datalinks are separated from less important ones to reduce the risk of hacking. 

Phalanx ground-based systems in the south defend the air from artillery barrages. The predictable trajectories of artillery shells are quickly gunned down by the gatling guns along with its interceptor rockets. The F-16s trade fire, dropping 5000 lb JDAM guided dumb bombs onto the artillery positions while defended by its strike group. 

F-16s continue their strikes onto the ill-planned Bobian attack with continued bombardment using anti-personnel cluster munitions. Infantry fighting vehicles on the ground continue to use their 30 mm autocannons to mow down the survivors. 

The armored vehicles continue their advance into the Bobian exclave with the support of airpower. 

(OOC: The soviet wave tactics don't make it across the border. I think this assessment should be uncontroversial as its essentially a militia with small arms trying to charge a conventional force. Also it's kinda reliant on the entire Reichswehr being oblivious to the approach even when weve been massing troops there for months and have UAVs in the area on top of spy satellites.)[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Operation Seesturm[/b]]

Following the suppression of enemy air defenses, buildup of supplies, surge exercises and movement of troops(https://www.nationstates.net/page=rmb/postid=59970203) Operation Seesturm would begin in full. Satellite, drone and radar had been used over the years to compile a list of the most promising landing zones. A total of three would be chosen: Eichenhafen, Schwarzwasser and Dünenfels. 

In preparation for the attack, the Kaiserreich would move to assert naval and air superiority in the theater. J-15Es, taking off from the mainland would use their Gunslinger missiles to engage Bobian jets from before visual range. The missiles, using a wide range of guidance from the radars on the jets themselves, ground-based systems and ships are provided a constant stream of data to maintain locks on their targets. Speeding to mach 3, the interceptors reach exceedingly high speeds to avoid interception while their electronic countermeasures help prevent spoofing and jamming. However, that wouldnt be the only challenge facing Bobian jets. FAS-3s, with a range of 170 kilometers would use their hypersonic proximity-fused interceptors against Bobian aircraft and missiles. 

After the suppression of enemy air defenses, the show would begin. Donnerkeil cruise missiles, available in large quantities from the mainland, would be launched into Bobian airspace. Their terrain tracking would allow them to stay low to the ground to avoid radar detection and thus interception. On top of this their tiny radar cross section would maintain further stealth capabilities. Upon nearing their targets the missiles release clouds of chaff to create decoys for enemy radar. These missiles are poised to strike a wide range of targets critical to the Bobian war effort: arms depots, roads, strategic factories, command centers, artillery and coastal defences. 

All the while, the J-16CJs and their strike packages maintaining positions at before visual range. Their targeting systems and that of their REG-3000 anti-radiation missiles are looking for any radar activation. Should any anti-air be used against the airstrikes the missiles would know their location and quickly lock on to destroy them. 

Ground based jamming systems are utilized against the Bobians as well. Barrage jamming is used to send large amounts of static across a large range of frequencies to break down communications among the Bobians. DFRM is utilized as well. Using this tactic the Kaiserreich intercepts radar transmissions, alters them and then sends them out again with the purpose of creating false targets, communications and others to degrade the ability of the Bobians to respond. 

Naval gunfire also pounds the Bobian defences. Hundreds of Donnerkeil missiles, which skim above the water to avoid detection, are used to hit coastal defences in a massed saturation attack. Along with the Donnerkeils flies the TK-300 which provides both jamming and decoys to waste Bobian interceptors.  

At the break of dawn following days of airstrikes meant to wear down the Bobian defenses Operation Seesturm starts its early stages. UUVs, underwater unmanned vehicles, are used to clear the strait of enemy mines to allow for a landing. The Reichswehrs ships are also degaussed to reduce the risk of attack from magnetic field triggered mines. Escort ships combined with mainland defenses provide air cover over the Marineinfantriekorps units as they move forward. LCACs loaded with several expeditionary units, AAVs, supplies and tanks are driven towards the landing zones. 

At 0600 at Eichenhafen landing zone, the first AAVs roll onto Bobian territory.[/spoiler]

[quote=technokratisches_kaiserreich;60000681][spoiler=[b]Eastern Shamat Theater Operations[/b]][i]The Hydronian air force would again underestimate the Donnerkeils. Tiny radar cross sections and low altitude would allow the missiles to blend into the terrain easily even if it is flat making it nearly impossible to differentiate from the ground. The beam width of the look down radar would also limit them. The missiles traveling at 900 km/h would only spend brief periods in the beam width allowing for minimal time and minimal detection. Doppler filtering used by the aircrafts radar to distinguish has a velocity gate making it susceptible to cross-moving missiles. The missiles would continue towards their targets with minimal interception. 

The Hydronians had also forgotten about the Reichswehrs J-15Es specifically designed for anti-air engagements. AESA radar allow the J-15s to quickly acquire multiple targets and lock on. Gunslinger BVRAAMs would launched towards the enemy at before visual range. Dozens of other radar in the Reichswehr including ships, fighter jets and ground based would feed data into these missiles to maximize interceptions. However, another group of J-15Es would engage the enemy as well. Using their IRST capabilities they would be able to lock onto the enemy without any warning. While the aircraft attempt to avoid the Gunslingers another round of BVRAAMs are launched from the other squadrons. 

Acoustic guidance used by the Hydronians is a terrible method of tracking. The quiet hum of drone propellers would easily be drowned out by the supersonic missiles making acoustic tracking extremely hard. The limited resolution of acoustic systems would make it very hard to pinpoint the direction and location of the drones especially when using missile interceptors. Most likely it would be a massive waste of money as the drones continue to attack Hydronian radar. 

Rapid deceleration of a missile going at mach 6 paints a massive target on the missiles. During cruise phase the missile generated massive amounts of heat by going at mach 6 making its direction, location and speed obvious to infrared tracking. Now that it slowed down the interceptors would be fired. FAS-3 SAMs would be deployed using their kinetic kill vehicles and high-G maneuvering capabiltiies to destroy the interceptors. Raketes from the fleet would also be launched to intercept the now slowed down missiles. 

ATTs would largely cover the fleet from the submarine attacks but the Reichswehr would still have to deal with the enemy submarines. The Reichswehrs torpedoes would largely be effective. Jamming wouldnt be effective as the torpedoes constantly hop frequencies to avoid jamming. The submarines desperate attempts to maneuver wouldnt help. The inherently much larger cross section of the enemies submarines would be a large target for the Reichswehrs subs. If that didnt deal with the enemy the UUV swarms would be dropped into the depths. These autonomous vehicles utilizing torpedoes would swarm submarines, each of the drones costing less than the torpedoes used to intercept them. Using swarm tactics and overwhelming firepower they aim to destroy the enemy subs. 

REG-3000s would continue on target towards the enemy radar using INS to find the locations of the radars despite disruption attempts. The Kaiserliche Marines UUVs are dispatched underwater to dismantle the enemies water pressure mines. Using LF-SAS the UUVs locate the mines and neutralize them to allow the safe passage of the ships. 

Naval gunfire and air power would be used to push the machine gunners and snipers back. JDAMs and cluster munitions would be dropped by J-16s onto the enemy on the ground while several Donnerkeil cruise missiles are launched at Hydronian forces from the fleet offshore. The gunfire of the 30 mm autocannons on the AAVs open up on the machine gunners and snipers with the crew using remote controlled systems to avoid taking fire. The vast majority of personnel in the Marineinfantriekorps would be carried via AAV protecting them from the small arms fire. 

The LCACs although large would be highly maneuverable. The landing cushions are able to reach speeds of 45+ knots to maneuver to avoid anti-ship missiles. Chaff is also deployed by the LCACs to create false signatures and mislead the enemy missiles. Nulkas would also be used to decieve the missiles and lead them away. 

The man portable anti armor missiles would destroy two AAVs on the beach, however, the multitude of defense systems wielded by Kaiserreich armor would protect the majority and allow them to continue forward. Explosive reactive armor would allow those that were hit to absorb and disrupt shaped charges. On top of this active protection systems would protect the vehicles. Radar and IR systems detect the incoming missiles and quickly launch their counter munitions. Jammers, smoke grenades and laser dazzlers are also used to mislead the missiles. The openly visible missile launchers would become a target as autocannons, tanks and fighter jets open up on their positions. The enemy aircraft wouldnt even get within range of the J-16s. Reichswehr control of the air through the destruction of the enemies last AA systems would give them free reign. Long before they would even reach the J-16s, FAS-3 hypersonic interceptors open up on them along with J-15E gunslinger interceptors. 

Despite the heavy resistance the operation continues. Armored vehicles with their defenses and combined with overwhelming airpower would continue to bring the thousands of Reichswehr troops further and further into Hydronia. By the third day, a total of 70,000 troops had been brought to eastern Hydronia mainly through sealift. Now, however, the soldiers werent just from the Kaiserreich they were a multi-nation coalition assembled by the EDU. Constant sealift of supplies to the fleet and the occupied territory would be provided by EDU escorts and supply ships. Underway replenishment along with TRAM would be carried out to resupply the Kaiserreichs forces. As man-portable missiles head for the A-20 and helicopters the countermeasures deploy. Flares are deployed to deceive infrared trackers while directional infrared countermeasures are used to blind or jam the missile seeker. Using terrain masking the helicopters are low to the ground in order to avoid radar detection while their early warning systems allow them to take evasive maneuvers as well as use their countermeasures. An engine aboard an attack helicopter is hit by a man portable missile and the helicopter goes down onto a nearby hill. The others, however, survive and continue their personnel insertion and airstrike missions. 

(set before the landing)

The paratroopers had jumped from the K-130s at night to reduce the visibility of the machine gunners on the ground. While this would run the risk of dropping into unintended areas it would also make it very difficult to spot the men as they jumped. The pilots themselves approach the landing zones using nap-of-the earth to avoid radar detection. Multiple LZs located behind enemy lines would help minimize the chances of mass interception while dummies would also be used to create decoys. MRZR light military vehicles air dropped in with the paratroopers would accompany the men on their missions. These light vehicles allow the men to traverse terrain quickly to capture intersections, bridges, airfields and sabotage the enemy. [/i][/spoiler]

[nation]Ekpatanus[/nation]
[nation]United Hydronia[/nation][/quote]

[spoiler=[b]defending[/b]]
After failure to intercept the majority of the missiles, the ornate squadron would be rerouted to the east to aid in defending the skies during the ongoing landing. Small air defence systems situated at Military targets would fire surface-to-air interceptors at the Donnerkeil missiles as they approached, hoping to minimise damage, but oil refineries and other infrastructure would take heavy hits.

Jamming and chaff spraying would be employed to help protect the Hydronians against the incoming missiles. As the jets took evasive action, jamming would attempt to disable the missiles and chaff would attempt to confuse their radar. As the submarines in the water continued to take down the Kaiserreichs fleet, the missiles would become less and less accurate due to less information inputs. These tactics would be employed to deal with both rounds of missiles simultaneously, but at least 2 jets would be downed.

Despite appearing like a ridiculous idea, these acoustic-guided missiles are more useful than they seem. Due to their already close proximity to the drones when being released, it is far easier for them to lock onto them. This is greatly aided by the incredibly sensitive fine tuning of the sensors. Whilst this is still an experimental technology, it does have its uses.

The Mach 6 missiles high manoeuvrability due to light weight and thrust nozzles would allow them to avoid the interceptors relatively easily. Their ability to reaccelerate would then come into play. Once it had avoided the interceptors it would lock back onto the jets with their laser homing and speed back up to Mach 6 to quickly take down the jets.

The Kaiserreich used ATTs to attempt to cover their fleet from the submarine attacks, but they would not be so successful. Due to the torpedoes being launched almost directly underneath the  kaiserreichs ships, the torpedoes would be very hard to intercept. They essentially used the technocratic fleet as cover from their own weapons and sonars. The window to detect and launch interceptors is very small from such proximity and so it would be difficult for the Kaiserreich to launch ATTs quick enough and accurately enough. Most of the torpedoes would continue towards their targets as the submarines continued their tactics of staying deep in the water to avoid detection, then rising up directly underneath ships to release their payload, before diving back down into the depths of the North Sea.

The enemy torpedoes would be dealt with by Hydronias ATTs. The enemy subs would be dealt with by the same torpedoes used to destroy the fleet. The submarines would fire small, agile torpedoes towards the swarming UUVs, whilst taking evasive action. These torpedoes would work to intercept the swarm, whilst using jamming tactics to misguide the UUVs.

The highly sensitive mines would be set off by even the slightest pressure change. Some of the mines would be set off as the UUVs approached them, but others would end up being safely dismantled, allowing the ship through. The Radar would take heavy hits, with nearly all of it being disabled. This wouldnt concern the Hydronians too much however as they had already served their purpose.

Despite small fire doing nothing to the AAVs, Hydronias firework-3400 man-portable missile launchers would be employed to destroy the approaching AAVs and other armoured vehicles. Huge numbers of these missiles would be fired towards the landing party, it would be impossible to intercept them all. The firework-3400s would also be loaded with small interceptor missiles. Multitudes of these would be fired towards the Donnerkeils to help protect the troops as well as into the sky against the jets. The JDAMs and cluster bombs would do heavy damage to the Hydronian infantry. The machine gunners and snipers would be able to take cover behind hills to avoid the incoming fire.

Since the missiles failed to deal significant damage to the LCACs, the machine gunners up in the hills would be given orders to also target the LCACs.

The missiles would continue to fire at the AAVs. Huge numbers of the missiles would be used to overwhelm the enemy. They couldnt all be intercepted. Due to the portable nature of the missile launchers, they would be moved behind the protective hills before anything could hit them. They would continue to fire from behind the hills.

The Kaiserreich jets had reacted too late. Air-to-air missiles were already well on their way towards the jets. Interceptors open up on the Hydronian missiles, but due to their relative cheapness compared to hypersonic missiles, huge barrages of then would be fired to exhaust the enemy of their interception capabilities. The jets would take evasive action whilst using jamming devices to avoid the enemys attempts to take them down.

The Kaiserreichs supply lines had so far seemed unstoppable, but Hydronias earlier mentioned submarine tactics would deal with that. As new ships approached the speedy submarines would begin targeting them too, launching barrages of torpedoes from underneath.

The countermeasures against the missiles would do a good job for the most part, except for one major flaw. The size of the aircraft compared to the missiles would allow them to continue in the same direction and hit the aircraft, despite the lack of targeting capabilities. Damage would be lower than the Hydronians wished, but it would still hinder the Kaiserreich.

[i]- BEFORE THE LANDING -[/i]

Spotting the paratroopers as they jumped would prove difficult due to the time of day, but the machine gunners had adopted a tactic of simply spraying bullets throughout the air to maximise the amount of troops they could stop before they hit the ground. The high number of machine gunners present would allow this tactic to work well, with bullets filling the night sky. Any soldiers who landed in unintended areas would be shot on sight to swiftly eliminate any threat they posed. As the enemy troops used their vehicles to quickly attempt to sabotage Hydronian targets, they would be stopped. As they approached airfields and other locations, huge numbers of Hydronian troops would be waiting. Earlier, Hydronian scouts had spotted the helicopters and both notified the machine gunners and nearby bases similar. The Hydronian numbers would be able to quickly surround and overwhelm the small in comparison Kaiserreich teams.
[/spoiler]
